transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-07-30 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (Clarion Head of ML), Samir Khan (Clarion SRE), Ellen Price (Clarion Product)

Summary notes auto-section (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Demo of Console 'Request Inspector' and 'Request Playback'
- Showed trace -> request mapping, error funnel analysis, and how to export request logs for offline debugging
- Discussed pilot and security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got Alex and Priya from Redwood. How's it going Maya?
[00:09] Maya: Hey Alex, hey Priya, good, thanks. Samir just joined a minute ago. Trying to debug a recent spike in hallucinations in prod so looking forward to seeing the request playback stuff.
[00:20] Priya: Awesome, we'll try to keep it hands-on. Quick agenda: request-inspector demo, trace mapping, error hunting patterns, then export and pilot next steps.
[00:30] Samir: Quick note, we care about 95th pct latency under 300ms for short prompts, and also need audit logs for compliance.
[00:40] Alex: Great — we'll point out the audit + export features. Okay Priya, over to you.
[00:45] Priya: Cool. I'm sharing the Console now. So this is the Requests view, you can filter by model, route, client id... 
[01:10] Priya: Here's a sample error spike — you can see an anomaly in error rate at approx 10:12 UTC. We can click into a trace id, and the request inspector will show the full prompt, token counts, runtime logs, and any fallback decisions.
[01:40] Ellen: I like the playback bit — can we reproduce the same model outputs when we replay? Like is it deterministic?
[01:50] Priya: Good question. Playback respects model version and seed where applicable, but nondeterministic behavior can still occur for non-deterministic sampling. We do enable a 'fixed seed' option on the playback UI to make runs as close as possible for debugging. Note: for some quantized variants small differences happen.
[02:10] Maya: And does playback re-run through customer data plane for Private deployments or stays in Redwood sandbox?
[02:20] Priya: For hosted we replay within our inference runtime; for Private we provide a playback agent that runs inside your VPC so logs and secrets never leave your network — that's in the private deployment docs.
[02:40] Samir: Ok that helps. On the trace id mapping, sometimes our tracing tool shows spans split across many requests, can Request Inspector join them?
[02:55] Priya: Yes, we surface parent/child relationships. You can drop in your trace id from Jaeger/Zipkin and we attempt to correlate using common identifiers; occasional mismatches if instrumentation differs — we do fuzzy matching and show a confidence score.
[03:20] Alex: Note that sometimes transcript offsets or tokenization naming is garbled in auto-transcript — so Priya might refer to KV "cash" in the UI but it's KV cache.
[03:35] Priya: haha yes — the ASR is not perfect. Moving on, here's a failed request — status 500 with a model truncate error. The inspector shows the kernel selection logs, early OOM, and the fallback policy triggered to a smaller context window.
[03:55] Maya: Wait which fallback? We thought that was off for our account.
[04:00] Priya: On your tenant we have a soft fallback enabled for safety so that if a request exceeds memory it falls back to a quantized smaller variant to preserve availability. It's toggleable via the rollout config.
[04:20] Samir: Can we see the raw request logs — like the exact byte stream and headers?
[04:25] Priya: Yep, Request Inspector has an Export button. You can export as JSON lines with trace id, timestamps, token counts, returned logits snippets, and any runtime warnings.
[04:40] Ellen: That JSON export — is it S3 push or can we pull via API?
[04:45] Priya: Both. We can schedule push to your S3 bucket (Private use may require VPC peering or gateway) or you can hit the Logs Export API.
[04:55] Maya: When you say 'returned logits snippets' is that safe to share?
[05:00] Priya: We redact certain sensitive fields on hosted exports depending on retention and privacy settings; for Private it's controlled by you. We'll include a redaction checklist in the runbook.
[05:15] Alex: Quick technical deep dive, people often mix up prefix caching vs KV caching. Priya, want to show the timeline where caching helped latency?
[05:27] Priya: Sure. So here's a high-throughput route, we can visualize request timeline; notice the steady latency drop after enabling prefix cache — because repeated prompts hit the cached prefix and skip the early layers. KV cache is different — that's the per-session key-value cache for autoregressive continuation.
[05:50] Maya: Hmm earlier we saw a weird latency spike even with prefix cache on — could that be batching?
[06:00] Priya: Yes, batching can increase P99 if batch windows wait for more requests. Our console shows batch sizes and tunable max latency. For low-latency SLOs you adjust max batch wait or prioritize low-latency lanes.
[06:20] Samir: What about quantization — if we move to int8 variants will that change token-level determinism and cause our hallucination regression?
[06:30] Priya: Potentially; quantization can slightly change logits distribution. That's why Redwood Optimize recommends canarying quantized variants with a small eval set — the Console ties quality regressions to prompt sets so you can track if hallucination rate climbs post-quantize.
[06:55] Ellen: Can you show an example of quality regression alerting?
[07:00] Priya: Sure — here's the Quality dashboard; we tied a prompt set 'diagnosis-summaries' and after a rollout to quantized-v2 we saw a rise in incorrect factuals. The Console surfaces the top failing prompts and example diffs.
[07:20] Maya: Very helpful. Back to debugging — what about cross-request correlation for multi-turn flows?
[07:30] Priya: The Request Inspector threads multi-turn by session id. Sometimes your SDK rewrites session ids; we capture both the SDK session and the HTTP session headers to help correlate.
[07:50] Alex: We should call out costs — replaying at scale is compute-heavy. We can replay a small sample deterministically; full replays might incur charges.
[08:00] Priya: Yup, and for pilot we usually recommend sampling 1-2% of traffic or focusing on the problematic window.
[08:15] Samir: For the pilot we want to run a 48h replay of a 24h window to simulate peak. Would Redwood support that?
[08:25] Alex: Yes, with Dedicated or Private options we'd provision a temporary burst cluster. We'll include a pricing estimate for that.
[08:40] Maya: Security — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, and KMS integration. Where do we find docs?
[08:48] Alex: I'll send the SOC2 summary and SSO/KMS integration guide. We also support audit log retention settings in the Console.
[09:00] Priya: Back to the UI, here's a request with an unusual rerank fallback. The reranker scored low and we fell back to a cached response. You can see in the inspector both the rerank score and the fallback policy reason.
[09:25] Ellen: How do we link that rerank event to the original indexing pipeline?
[09:30] Priya: We inject trace metadata — if your indexing pipeline attaches the same correlation id we map it. Otherwise there is heuristics.
[09:45] Maya: Are there any dashboard alerts we should set for error spikes?
[09:50] Priya: Yes, you can set per-route alerts for error rate, latency percentiles, and quality regressions; they can integrate with PagerDuty or Slack.
[10:05] Samir: In our infra we use Prometheus and want to scrape metrics — supported?
[10:10] Priya: Yep, we export Prom-compatible metrics via an endpoint in Dedicated/Private, and hosted can push to your ingestion pipeline.
[10:20] Alex: Let's demo a concrete error hunt — Priya, walk through the 10:12 spike.
[10:25] Priya: Sure. I'm filtering to that window. You can see a cluster of 500s corresponding to requests with long context length and a kernel selection warning — runtime chose a slower kernel due to sequence length and bumped memory.
[10:45] Priya: Clicking into one trace, the inspector shows tokenized prompt, attention matrix summary (we only show condensed), and a runtime line: "evicting kv cache due to memory pressure" — that's probably why continuation produced odd outputs.
[11:05] Maya: That matches our observation — multi-document prompts from the search pipeline are pushing sequence length up. Can we truncate automatically or rewrite prompts?
[11:15] Priya: You can enforce per-route max_tokens and server-side truncation strategies; Console shows the truncation points and any warnings. Also Optimize suggests chunking long docs and server-side compression heuristics.
[11:35] Samir: If truncation is applied will that be visible in logs so QA can see where content was dropped?
[11:40] Priya: Yes, truncation metadata is included in the export so you know which tokens were removed.
[11:50] Ellen: About redaction — if we export logs for your team will PHI be redacted automatically?
[11:57] Priya: On hosted we redaction is configurable; for healthcare customers we recommend Private deployment and then you control redaction policies. We'll include the redaction config sheet.
[12:10] Alex: Quick side note: some names might be mis-transcribed here, e.g. "Jaeger" might become "Jagger" in the ASR.
[12:20] Priya: ok switching to Request Playback feature — you can pick a trace id and hit Replay. Here's a small replay window, choose 'fixed seed' and 'hosted vs private agent' options.
[12:45] Priya: Running replay now — shows per-step latency, model selection, and any runtime anomalies. You can step through tokens or jump to the runtime log where the OOM was thrown.
[13:05] Maya: Nice. The token-by-token step is great for finding when hallucination starts.
[13:10] Priya: Exactly — and you can diff two replays side-by-side, which is helpful when comparing quantized vs fp16 runs.
[13:25] Samir: If we wanted to automate replay for failing prompts nightly is there an API?
[13:30] Priya: Yes, there's a Replay API and a scheduler. We'll add rate limits and quota guardrails to prevent accidental mass replays.
[13:45] Ellen: Any gotchas for replaying encrypted payloads?
[13:50] Priya: Payload decryption must occur within your environment for Private; hosted requires that you have given permission for Redwood to decrypt for the purpose of replay. We log any access.
[14:05] Alex: Let's show the logs export flow: select traces -> export -> choose S3 or API -> choose redaction level -> deliver.
[14:20] Priya: Demonstrating now — exporting a 2h window as ndjson to S3. It shows approximate size and estimated cost for retrieval.
[14:40] Maya: Good to see cost estimate. For pilot budgeting, can you provide a line-item for replay compute?
[14:45] Alex: Yes we'll include that in the SOW.
[14:50] Priya: Now quick note about trace correlation with external APMs: we can propagate trace context headers. If you instrument upstream, our console will link to your APM like Datadog or New Relic when the trace id matches.
[15:10] Samir: Is the matching exact or fuzzy?
[15:15] Priya: Exact if your trace id is present; fuzzy if not. We also surface step names and approximate timestamps to assist manual correlation.
[15:35] Maya: Walk me through an example of a rerun where model variant selection changed the output — I want to be sure this is visible.
[15:45] Priya: Ok, replay of two runs: one to quantized-v1 and one to fp16. The diff viewer highlights differences at token level and we attach a quality score delta.
[16:05] Ellen: Can you export that diff as a CSV for our QA team?
[16:10] Priya: Yep — diffs and flagged prompts exportable.
[16:20] Samir: We have strict retention rules — how long do request logs live by default?
[16:25] Priya: Default is 30 days on hosted, configurable longer for enterprise. Private you manage retention.
[16:35] Maya: Ok, for compliance we need 1 year of logs in immutable storage — possible?
[16:40] Alex: For Dedicated/Private yes, with archive to S3 Glacier or your storage. We'll cover that in the contract.
[16:55] Priya: Quick performance note: the Console shows kernel warnings like "fused-attention fall back" — that often points to unsupported op or sequence length that triggers slower kernel paths.
[17:10] Maya: If we see fused to slow kernel frequently can Redwood tune the runtime?
[17:15] Priya: Our runtime team can recommend model variants or compilation flags; for Dedicated we can apply custom kernel selection policies.
[17:30] Alex: Time check — ~35 minutes in. Any other deep technical asks?
[17:36] Samir: Can we run a smoke test to validate our integration? Maybe a simple tracer that sends sample requests and verifies trace propagation?
[17:45] Priya: We have a smoke test script and a quickstart repo. I'll drop links.
[17:55] Ellen: Also want a concise guide for where to find the rollback controls in the Console in case a rollout causes a quality regression.
[18:05] Priya: Rollbacks and canaries are under the Deployments tab; you can rollback one click or promote a canary to global. We'll include a screenshot.
[18:20] Maya: For the pilot, if we test quantized variants how do we ensure prompt sets represent clinical language?
[18:30] Priya: You upload custom prompt sets and associated scores; Console ties eval runs to those sets. We can help seed a prompt set from Clarion's sample docs.
[18:45] Samir: Any integration with our CI/CD? We want alerts in PRs for quality regressions.
[18:50] Priya: You can POST eval results as a webhook and fail CI if thresholds exceed. Many teams integrate with GitHub Actions.
[19:05] Alex: Two quick security clarifications from earlier: SAML SSO is supported, and KMS integration for key wrapping is supported for Private and – with caveats – for Dedicated. I'll send details.
[19:20] Maya: Do you have a contact for legal on data processing addendum?
[19:25] Alex: Yes, I'll cc legal and put DPA template in our follow-up.
[19:35] Priya: Wrapping up, demo re: request-inspector: we've shown how to trace error -> request -> token timeline -> replay -> export.
[19:50] Ellen: Great — feels like this covers the main asks.
[19:55] Samir: For the sample logs — what's the recommended format?
[20:00] Priya: NDJSON with fields: trace_id, timestamp, route, model, token_count, runtime_warnings, raw_prompt, redaction_flags. We'll share a sample.
[20:15] Alex: Let's capture explicit next steps: Redwood will send SOC2, SSO/KMS doc; Priya will share runbook; Clarion will supply logs and SLOs. Pilot SOW to be drafted.
[20:30] Maya: Sounds good. Any remaining questions?
[20:35] Ellen: One quick: trial keys for the pilot — do you need anything from our side?
[20:40] Alex: We'll provision keys once SOW is signed; for Private we might need a narrow set of infra details. We'll follow up with a short checklist.
[20:52] Priya: Alright I'm dropping the runbook and quickstart links in chat now.
[21:00] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the benchmark.

(End of recorded transcript — remainder of call was scheduling logistics and off-record Q&A.)

Notes about transcription quality: occasional ASR errors (e.g., "KV cash" vs "KV cache", "Jagger" vs "Jaeger"). Some speaker labels were generic.
